title: Radioactivity and Nuclear Decay
text: Radioactivity is the spontaneous emission of radiation from unstable atomic nuclei. There are three main types of radioactive decay: alpha decay, which emits helium-4 nuclei; beta decay, which emits electrons or positrons; and gamma decay, which emits high-energy photons. Henri Becquerel discovered radioactivity in 1896, and Marie Curie and Pierre Curie conducted pioneering research on the phenomenon. The rate of radioactive decay is characterized by the half-life, the time it takes for half of a radioactive sample to decay. Radioactivity has applications in medicine (cancer treatment, medical imaging), power generation, and dating of ancient materials through radiocarbon dating.
